title: MCM-41 loading-dependent ZnO nanocomposites for efficient photocatalytic degradation of methylene blue and rhodamine B
content: The discharge of synthetic dyes into aquatic environments represents a significant environmental challenge due to their chemical stability, persistence, and potential ecological impacts. Although zinc oxide (ZnO) is considered a promising semiconductor photocatalyst for wastewater treatment, its practical performance is limited by particle aggregation, restricted surface accessibility, and rapid recombination of photogenerated charge carriers. In this study, mesoporous MCM-41 was incorporated into ZnO to improve its physicochemical characteristics and photocatalytic performance toward methylene blue (MB) and rhodamine B (RhB) degradation. Pure ZnO and MCM-41/ZnO nanocomposites containing 1, 3, and 5 wt% MCM-41 were synthesized using a sol–gel impregnation method and calcined at 500 °C. The prepared materials were characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and UV-visible diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (UV-vis DRS). The effects of solution pH, photocatalyst dosage, initial dye concentration, and MCM-41 loading on photocatalytic performance were systematically investigated under UV-visible irradiation, together with degradation kinetics and catalyst reusability. The optimized 3 wt% MCM-41/ZnO (3MZ) nanocomposite exhibited an apparent optical band gap of 2.94 eV, compared with 3.20 eV for pure ZnO. Photocatalytic performance was evaluated by monitoring the decrease in the characteristic UV-vis absorption bands of MB and RhB. Using 0.050 g of catalyst in 50 mL of dye solution (1.0 g L−1), at an initial dye concentration of 10 mg L−1, the 3MZ nanocomposite achieved apparent decolorization efficiencies of 97.70% for MB after 50 min at pH 8 and 94.50% for RhB after 180 min at pH 4 under UV-visible irradiation. The photocatalytic degradation behavior was adequately described by an apparent pseudo-first-order kinetic model. Furthermore, reusability experiments demonstrated that the 3MZ nanocomposite maintained apparent degradation efficiencies of 88.1% for MB and 86.7% for RhB after four reuse cycles, indicating promising operational stability.
